davinci.why_station: renders and GPU finishing run on the VIDEO STATION RTX A5000 (much faster than the laptop i7-9750H); the bridge --host station default routes there. The laptop route stays as an offline fallback.
davinci.mcp_tools: 14 (run_script sandboxed Python 3.14 over the full scripting API, API search/docs, LUT/DCTL authoring)

station.note: media is mirrored to the station by station_archive (studio.py archive-push) before finishing; the bridge remaps the sequence.xml pathurls from the local production root to <archive root>/<slug>

community_mcp.name: davinci-resolve-community-station
community_mcp.why_on: user asked (2026-09-22) for the ready compound workflows available at any moment: rough cut from raw footage, media analysis with transcription, offline .drp/.drt/.drx editing, conform QC, and destructive-op safety traps that the official 14-tool server does not have
community_mcp.station_wrapper: <station>/resolve-community-mcp.cmd (sets RESOLVE_SCRIPT_API/LIB + PYTHONUNBUFFERED, runs venv python -u src/server.py, 37 compound tools)
community_mcp.contextual_loading: ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH is on, so the 37 compound tools are deferred: a names-only list in-session, near-zero cost until used. Per request, decide the Resolve domain and ToolSearch only the relevant compound tool(s) — do not resident-load the whole server. Domain->tool map in references/davinci-resolve.md.
community_mcp.context_cost: full resident load would be ~142 KB/session; deferred under Tool Search it is names-only until a tool is searched
community_mcp.domain_skills_root: <davinci-resolve-mcp>/.claude/skills (craft docs written for this server's tool names; also mirrored on the station under <station>/davinci-resolve-mcp/.claude/skills)
community_mcp.laptop_copy: <davinci-resolve-mcp> (v4.8.13, drives the laptop Resolve, kept but not registered live)

station_archive.policy: laptop is the working copy; every production is mirrored to the station after ingest, render and delivery; nothing is deleted on either side by tooling

antigravity.engine: Google AI Pro / Antigravity — Gemini 3.5 Flash (cloudcode id gemini-3-flash-preview)

commands.script: python scripts/antigravity.py script --brief BRIEF --out OUT [--duration N]
commands.analyze_shot: python scripts/antigravity.py analyze --media MP4 --kind shot --out OUT [--brief BRIEF] [--context TEXT]
commands.analyze_master: python scripts/antigravity.py analyze --media MASTER.mp4 --kind master --out OUT [--brief BRIEF]

antigravity.video_analysis: native Gemini video understanding via agy-cloudcode: up to 24 adaptive frames + ffmpeg audio -> whisper transcript, then Gemini. Requires node, ffmpeg and whisper on PATH.
antigravity.auth: OAuth from Windows Credential Manager gemini:antigravity via <claui-home>/get-agy-token.ps1 (no API key); project plasma-benefit-pgc82, tier g1-pro
antigravity.quota: consumes the user's Google AI Pro subscription; the bridge is invoked explicitly and never loops. agy-cloudcode already retries 429 with backoff.
antigravity.analyze_output: structured JSON: summary, brief/continuity/emotional read, defects, plus professional fixes[] (issue/why/priority) and per-tool editing guidance edit_blender[] (3D/compositing/PNG text/VSE) and edit_davinci[] (cut/grade/Fairlight/delivery), and a recommendation.
antigravity.advisory_rule: script output feeds the storyboard/plan; analyze output (including its fixes and editing guidance) is advisory evidence only, never creative acceptance — a human still watches and listens (same rule as review_shot.py).
antigravity.verified_live: 2026-09-23: script returned a 3-scene Hebrew JSON; analyze --kind shot returned parsed advisory JSON with a summary and recommendation on a real 3s clip.

tesseract.engine: Tesseract by Mirage (tsrct CLI 0.2.0), local Vulkan render engine
tesseract.why_station: the renderer crashes on the laptop CPU (i7-9750H, illegal instruction); it renders on the VIDEO STATION RTX A5000. Authoring + font prep run on the laptop, render runs on the station over SSH.

commands.title: python scripts/tesseract_overlay.py title --text T --font FONT --name SLUG --out-dir DIR [--canvas WxH] [--duration S] [--font-size N] [--fill r,g,b,a] [--overlay]

tesseract.hebrew_verified: 2026-09-23: renders Hebrew RTL + niqqud + bidi correctly (verified visually with Arial and the licensed Almoni brand font).
tesseract.brand_font_rule: the renderer only rasterizes TrueType and its matcher fails on family names with periods/spaces (e.g. 'Almoni Tzar DL 4.0 AAA'). The bridge normalizes any brand OTF/TTF to a clean ASCII-named TrueType before import (glyphs unchanged); requires otf2ttf + cu2qu (pip).
tesseract.output: editable .tsrct + preview PNG + export: opaque H.264 MP4, or with --overlay a transparent ProRes 4444 MOV (yuva444, alpha) to composite over footage in Blender or DaVinci.
tesseract.boundaries: supported-composition motion graphics and titles only: no 3D mesh/rigging (that stays Blender), no colour grading / Fairlight / delivery (that stays DaVinci). Text is native editable text here (unlike the Blender path which uses PNG), verified for Hebrew. Brand new (v0.2.0, 2026-09-23) — maturity risk.
tesseract.requirements: node/ffmpeg/whisper not needed; render needs the station GPU. Font prep needs local fonttools + otf2ttf + cu2qu.
tesseract.advisory_rule: a rendered frame is not creative acceptance; watch the motion. Composite output is a source layer, not a finished deliverable.

whatsapp.note: optional: final viewing copy delivered to your own WhatsApp; leave ssh_host empty to disable
